html:
Georgia is a country in the Caucasus, between the Black Sea and the Caspian. The map shows the medieval Kingdom of Georgia from 1200 to 1500, and the modern country from 1914 to 2010.

Its peoples had old kingdoms, Colchis on the coast and Iberia inland, and the conversion of Georgia to Christianity in the 300s made it one of the first Christian states. Bagrat III united the Georgian lands into one kingdom in 1008.

Its golden age came next:

  • David IV, the Builder, beat the Seljuk Turks at Didgori in 1121 and took Tbilisi the next year.
  • Queen Tamar, who ruled from 1184 to 1213, made Georgia the strongest power in the Caucasus.
  • In her time Shota Rustaveli wrote The Knight in the Panther's Skin, the national epic.

The Mongols overran the kingdom in the 1230s, and Timur invaded it several times around 1400. By the 1490s it had split into rival kingdoms and princedoms, fought over by the Ottomans and Safavid Iran. In 1801 Russia annexed the eastern kingdom, and the rest followed.

Georgia was independent from 1918 to 1921 and was then taken by the Soviet Red Army. Stalin was a Georgian, from the town of Gori. Georgia became independent again in 1991. It lost a short war with Russia in 2008, and Russian troops still hold Abkhazia and South Ossetia.
sum: Georgia is a country in the Caucasus, between the Black Sea and the Caspian. The map shows the medieval Kingdom of Georgia from 1200 to 1500, and the modern country from 1914 to 2010.
